{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=cognitive+architecture+models+for+long-term+preference+formation+versus+transient+behavior&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7126885\", \"title\": [\"Preference Heterogeneity versus Economic Incentives:What Determines Long-Term Care Arrangements in Europe?\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Care arrangements vary widely across families and countries. To understand why, wedevelop a tractable static bargaining model of family long-term-care choices and estimateit using European data. Families choose among child-provided informal care,including which child becomes the caregiver, formal home care, mixed care, and nursing-homecare, taking into account both monetary costs and heterogeneous non-monetarypreferences over care arrangements. Preference heterogeneity strongly dampens policyresponsiveness: without it, a 20% subsidy to nursing-home and formal-home-care costsraises the use of formal care by 7.5%, compared with only 4.0% in the baseline model.Cross-country differences in care arrangements are shaped more by non-monetary factorsthan by formal-care prices. Looking ahead, the model predicts a substantial increasein demand for formal care by 2050, driven by a declining ratio of adult children toelderly parents, with the largest increases in countries where informal care is currentlypredominant.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7126885\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.5204/thesis.eprints.268426\", \"title\": [\"Long-Term Generative Models for Multimodal Behavior in Soccer\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This thesis develops deep learning algorithms for modelling long-term behaviours in soccer, spanning both continuous player and ball motion and the discrete actions that structure a match. These models address two long-standing industry-level challenges: collecting complete trajectories across all televised games, and labelling actions in those games in a semi-automated manner. The methods developed in this thesis have been deployed commercially, substantially increasing the scale and efficiency of soccer data collection.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.5204/thesis.eprints.268426\"}, {\"DOI\": \"10.21511/imfi.18(2).2021.18\", \"title\": [\"Investment behavior of short-term versus long-term individual investors of PAN India – An empirical study\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Investment activity, followed by household and external savings, often plays a decisive role in strengthening the financial status of individual investors, as it contributes to further increases in wealth. This study analyzes the investors’ investment motives and actions to find better investment strategies and to do a systematic review of the investment behavior available for both short- and long-term individual investors. The study is mainly focused on factors and priorities influencing investment decisions. The data were obtained using the questionnaire approach from 201 individual investors within the age group from 18 to 80 from different parts of India. Every individual investor’s risk-tolerant score has been calculated on the basis of the investors’ holistic behavior, namely, investors with high-risk appetite, investors with a moderate and low-risk appetite. Non-parametric tests are applied to evaluate the behavioral approach of investors that are differently correlated to these factors.
